method: A self-assessed rubric, not a measurement. Each subsystem has a weight (weights sum to 100). 'implemented' is the share of that subsystem's work that exists in any form, including approximations. 'verified' is the share whose behaviour has been confirmed identical to the original (bit for bit against its machine code, or exact by the loader/table layout in its code). The overall numbers are the weighted sums. The weights and shares are judgement calls and will change as work and understanding grow. The 2026-10-13 review raises the flight-model estimate from 76%/67% to 80%/71% for the recovered delta branch, full-element force composition, wing predicates, bounds writers and ordered grouping. These four-point changes are conservative judgement calls, not percentages derived from test counts. Kernel comparisons with controlled inputs, recorded CRT results or tolerances do not establish whole-simulator equivalence. The subsequent loader-fixture review keeps estimates unchanged: completed original-loader runs replace partial snapshots, but the current ACF object comparison is diagnostic, does not assert parity, and is explicitly ignored unless requested with local reference aircraft. The chord-loader review also keeps shares unchanged: one newly exact loader loop and its live inputs do not establish complete ACF loading or wing-coordinate parity. The boundary-writer review raises the flight-model rubric from 80%/71% to 81%/72%: the complete rib-coordinate loop and point transform are recovered and the live model now supplies their static ACF/CG inputs. This one-point change is a conservative judgement about a recovered geometry stage, not a percentage computed from 4293 compared words; dynamic state, curvature setup and whole trajectories remain unverified. The curvature-setup review keeps the rubric unchanged: the setup kernel has local original-code evidence, but its complete bounds input and live integration are still missing. Its local corpus is not distributed; the corresponding test is explicitly ignored unless requested. The body/gear reference-point review leaves estimates unchanged: two point-list producers now have exact local original-code comparisons, but runtime body grid preparation, propeller points and the complete reference-vector integration remain unfinished. Their original-code corpora are local and their comparisons are explicitly ignored in ordinary CI. The propeller reference-point review keeps estimates unchanged: the last identified point producer has local exact original-code evidence, but combined runtime state preparation and live reference-vector integration are not yet verified. The combined reference-geometry review keeps estimates unchanged: the ordered gear/wing/body/propeller vector and its final bounds now match a single original-code replay on explicit synthetic runtime state, but real-aircraft geometry preparation, auxiliary outputs and live integration remain unverified. Only allocator operations are replaced in that replay; its corpus stays local. The body-grid loader review raises the ACF rubric from 30%/10% to 32%/12% for the recovered complete grid conversion and strict checks on three actual aircraft. These two-point changes are conservative judgement, not percentages computed from coordinate counts. Full loader parity and UI/graphics parity remain unproven. The user explicitly requires whole-game X-Plane 12 parity 1:1. These weighted progress estimates are not completion evidence; the acceptance audit includes complete runtime behaviour and paired visual/motion comparisons. Overall parity remains unproven. The UI resource-loading review keeps all shares unchanged: original resources now load locally (25 menu textures and 12 font files), but no original menu state, layout, text rasterization or GPU output has been verified. The keyboard-table correction keeps shares unchanged: native loop bounds reveal 3138 command records and 182 default bindings including modifiers, correcting an incomplete 3012/71 catalogue. Local execution verifies key/mask copying, but native conflict handling, event dispatch and Alt/Esc menu handlers remain unresolved. The native key-vector loop review keeps shares unchanged: 2728 local original-code cases verify active/suppression transitions and ordered Begin/End requests with callback bodies replaced by loggers. Input gates, callback effects and live viewer integration are not verified; this is not whole input or UI parity. The menu-command routing review keeps shares unchanged: the native registration path and eight exact conditional helper traces establish main-menu/settings routing with six callee bodies replaced. Original query meanings, window services, Esc/Alt callbacks and rendering remain unverified; the request planner is not live UI. The window-state review keeps shares unchanged: 1033 controlled original-code contexts verify signed-kind lookup, window-list membership, parent opacity and both menu-command traces with only four action bodies logged. Real window creation, engine-state-byte lifecycle, renderer integration and paired captures are not verified.

subsystems.name: Aircraft files (ACF)
subsystems.note: All properties are preserved; typed: mass, CG, wings, gear, engine and controls subset. Loader schema recovered from the original; focused property subsets have strict original-code comparisons. Three original-loader replays now reach the return sentinel (13690, 13718 and 15525 tracked words). Previous fixtures were partial; two contain 424 corrected words each. These are reference results, not a count of matching ported fields. The full-object diagnostic is explicitly ignored by default, requires local reference files when requested, and reports remaining differences without asserting parity. The wing chord unit-conversion loop is enforced bit for bit on 312 synthetic original-code cases (3432 output words). Typed wings read all 48 slots and use supplied active rib chords; missing rib arrays retain a declared linear approximation. Active `_c_off_for_RIB` values are now typed without unit conversion and passed to the recovered boundary writer. The complete 20x18x3 body-grid feet conversion is recovered: 69120 synthetic SSE outputs and all 15120 supplied Cessna body-coordinate fields match exactly in debug/release. These local tests are explicitly ignored in ordinary CI; remaining full-object mismatches are still reported.

subsystems.name: 3D models (OBJ8)
subsystems.note: Geometry, nested transforms, rotation/translation animation, textures. No normal/lit maps, instruments, panels or most dynamic animation.

subsystems.name: Airfoil evaluation (AFL)
subsystems.note: All 34 airfoils; the whole profile function (selection, stall, buffet, blending, Mach factor) matches the original bit for bit on 1800 emulator cases.

subsystems.name: Flight model
subsystems.note: An approximate rigid-body model that takes off and flies. Verified against the original machine code in an emulator: the airfoil and per-element aerodynamics, the whole engine update and the propeller force function, the engine controls for every engine kind, the airflow wash, the terrain mesh probes (vertical ray and segment with moving cells), the strut, tire, wheel and body blend contact models, the weight and balance, the input binding query, and the whole flight step block by block: the wing, body and part loops, the landing gear (targets, steering, brakes, drag, strut contact), the wing and body ground contact chain, the hook, tow, float and wave forces, the plug-in force sink, the equations of motion and the integration, the position setter, the attitude, the geographic state, the 4 x 4 matrices and the Euler angles, the flight angles and the end of the step. Remaining recovery and integration work includes scenery-backed terrain and geoid queries, shared-pointer object lookups, per-strip airflow (`0x14121a9b0`), radiator update and runtime caller state; many ported blocks are not yet connected into a running model. The viewer still flies an approximate model, but now runs the recovered positive-delta coefficient branch and ordered wing grouping with recovered aspect/centroid parameters. Since the previous review, controlled original-code comparisons cover delta parameter curves, noise, target coefficients, full-element and force composition, aircraft bounds point emission, wing enable/join predicates and the 49-pass group scan. Full-element delta output matches 2099/2100 words exactly on macOS, with one platform-trigonometry difference checked by tolerance; some corpora use recorded CRT results or synthetic noise. Live wing chord inputs now use recovered ACF rib conversions and the typed reader scans 48 slots. The live boundary coordinates now use the recovered writer for up to ten elements, with ACF chord offsets and CG-relative origins. Dynamic wing rotation/retraction and aircraft curvature are fixed to zero; element force arms/normals and much of the running flight model remain approximate. Controlled whole-writer comparison covers 240 cases and 1431 points: all 4293 words match with recorded original CRT results, 4292 match using platform trigonometry (one bounded difference). Original geometry update scheduling, reference state and noise initialization are not yet connected. Curvature setup is recovered from acf/_ball_ang_def_deg: a local 521-case original-code comparison matches 1562/1563 words exactly, with one bounded platform-math difference. Live curvature remains zero until complete original reference bounds are supplied; the setup comparison is explicitly opt-in and its corpus is local. No whole-model parity is established. Body quad emission matches 47844 coordinate words across 120 local original-code cases; the ten-slot gear point pass matches 23952 words across 500 cases, both without tolerances. Inputs are explicit transformed body grids and stored gear fields, not proven live runtime state. Propeller point production now matches 28632 words across 400 local original-code cases, without tolerance. Gear, wing, body and propeller point producers are recovered individually; combined reference-vector assembly now matches 22350 point words and 800 final bounds words across 80 single-pass original-code cases. These checks include original auxiliary numerical helpers with only new/delete replaced; their auxiliary output fields are not compared. Body-grid/propeller runtime preparation and live reference integration remain unfinished.

subsystems.name: Datarefs and commands
subsystems.note: Registries and catalogs of 5503 datarefs and 3138 native command records from the original, its default keyboard map (182 bindings, 178 distinct chords, including Shift/Alt/Ctrl), values for 6 datarefs; 30 unmodified key commands act in the flight viewer; 2388 datarefs mapped to the field of the flight object or the simulation object that their getter reads (decoded from the getter code). All 182 key/mask pairs match a local original-code copy-block replay; four conflicting original chords are preserved and not dispatched. OS event lifecycle and UI handlers remain unverified. A separate native key-vector transition port matches 2728 local replay cases (active fields, suppression and ordered callback requests); callback bodies are logged, and live wiring is pending.

subsystems.name: Scenery and world
subsystems.note: Airport ground from apt.dat (runways, taxiways, aprons). No DSF, terrain, objects, lights or weather.

subsystems.name: Rendering
subsystems.note: wgpu viewer with lighting and glass. No PBR, shadows, sky, clouds or instrument screens. Original Alt/Esc UI is not ported in the active viewer: Esc exits, and its HUD uses Roboto Mono. No paired reference visual or motion comparison establishes UI/graphics fidelity. Original local UI resources now decode through ui-resources: 25 PNG/DXT5 DDS textures at their stored dimensions and 12 intact font files. The viewer is not yet connected to them; local decoding is not visual parity. Native controller/window-registry queries and cumulative parent opacity are recovered: 1033 local contexts match query results, finite opacity bits and 2066 command traces. Four UI action bodies remain logged; explicit state services are not yet live viewer UI.

subsystems.name: Platforms and distribution
subsystems.note: CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, nightly builds, standard folder layout. No launcher or settings UI.

roadmap.detail: ACF, OBJ8, AFL, apt.dat and the viewer work. Left: PANEL_3D, normal/lit maps, instruments, an apt.dat index. Verification work: turn the diagnostic ACF object comparison into enforced checks over explicitly supported fields, keep local reference diagnostics explicitly opt-in, and resolve differences against completed loader fixtures.

roadmap.title: Datarefs and commands
roadmap.detail: Registries and original catalogs exist. Left: values for the other 5497 datarefs, command handlers, wiring to the aircraft state.

roadmap.title: Flight model
roadmap.detail: Recovered profile, delta-wing, engine, propeller, contact and flight-step kernels exist with original-code comparisons. The approximate viewer now uses the delta branch and ordered wing grouping. The complete boundary coordinate loop and point transform now have original-code comparisons and run with static live inputs. Next: recover dynamic geometry state and full reference bounds, then connect the recovered curvature setup, original noise initialization and per-strip airflow; connect the remaining recovered force, propulsion and contact blocks into the runtime, then compare complete trajectories. Active rib chord values now come from ACF using the recovered conversion, and all 48 wing slots are scanned; dynamic geometry updates and force-arm/normal construction remain incomplete. Recovered body/gear point-list passes narrow the reference-bounds gap; propeller point production is now recovered too. The ordered main point vector and bounds reducer now match a single original-code pass on synthetic state. Next recover runtime body-grid and propeller field preparation, auxiliary outputs and the live geometry update schedule. Body-grid unit conversion now has exact checks on three real aircraft; runtime inclusion, normal generation and geometry scheduling remain work.

roadmap.title: World
roadmap.detail: Airport ground from apt.dat. Left: DSF terrain, library objects, lights, start locations, weather.

roadmap.title: Cockpit and systems

roadmap.title: Original UI and graphics fidelity
roadmap.detail: Original local resources load: 25 PNG/DXT5 DDS menu textures and 12 font files. Recover Alt/Esc handler state, font roles, layout, transitions and renderer behavior. Current viewer menus do not match the original. Require paired screenshots and GIF/video at identical resolution, settings and scene before claiming 1:1. Native default modifiers are recovered; Alt-only menu handling and original command callbacks remain unresolved. Main-menu/settings callback registration and conditional request order are recovered with explicit query returns; window-service bodies, live wiring and Esc handler remain unfinished. Window membership and cumulative opacity queries now execute natively in local combined checks; action bodies and state creation remain unfinished.

maintenance.goal: After substantial confirmed progress, review compatibility percentages against evidence, update this file and the roadmap, regenerate README.md and docs/COMPATIBILITY.md with python3 tools/compat_score.py --write, and push the site update. Always state verification limitations.
maintenance.percentage_policy: Keep estimates unchanged when new evidence improves verification quality without establishing broader behaviour coverage.
maintenance.publication: A push to main changing docs or README triggers the Pages workflow; check deployment outcome before claiming the live site is updated.
